lede: A month of housing law, coastal flood protection, local stormwater projects, balcony solar, northern New England wind, and a large private infrastructure commitment.

items.headline: Congress enacts the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
items.summary: The most significant federal housing package in three decades became law on July 11. It combines sixty provisions aimed at adding supply: zoning-reform guidance for cities, a broader definition of manufactured housing, and faster environmental review for small infill projects.

items.headline: Boston's coastal plan qualifies for a 65% federal cost share
items.summary: A U.S. Army Corps feasibility study opened the door to federal funding for Boston's roughly $10 billion coastal-resilience program. More than twenty projects along sixteen miles of shoreline are estimated to prevent $41 billion in flood damage.

items.headline: Queens turns roadway medians into stormwater sponges
items.summary: New York is spending $8.4 million to convert medians in Whitestone, Forest Hills, and Queens Village into planted green infrastructure. Together they are designed to capture about five million gallons of stormwater a year and cut combined-sewer overflows into nearby bays.

items.headline: California legislature legalizes plug-in balcony solar
items.summary: Lawmakers passed a bill that lets renters and owners install certified plug-in solar up to 1,200 watts in a standard outlet, without a rooftop rebuild. A few hundred watts can cover a fridge and modem; a full kit can run a window air conditioner on hot days.

items.headline: Maine advances a 1,200 MW line and 800 MW of onshore wind
items.summary: After years of delay, the Maine Public Utilities Commission selected Avangrid for a 1,200 MW transmission project that reuses existing corridors and Clearway for an 800 MW wind farm. Maine would take about 600 MW, with leftover capacity opened to later bids.

items.headline: Bank of America commits $250 billion to U.S. infrastructure finance
items.summary: On August 12 the bank launched an 18-month Critical Infrastructure Finance Initiative covering digital, energy, and core infrastructure through July 4, 2027. The headline is financing and advisory activity rather than a single grant, but it adds another large pool of private capital to grid, transport, and supply-chain buildout.
